exclude: Processor port and runtime scratch. Disk payloads .3, .4 and .5 load elsewhere.
BASIC system output on the loader snapshot, including the autostart load message.
Four gap bytes after the unconditional ladder-path jump. Neither table reference can index this high, and no exec, load or store watchpoint hit during the four stage-start probes.

Filled workspace tail after the name selector. RAM fill repeats across pages; the bounded actor, encounter and name arrays end before this range. No execute, load or store was observed in the four stage-start probes.
Load-tail bytes after the last score phrase terminates at $3FE7. No phrase pointer addresses this range.
Load-tail bytes after the paired terminator of the last gameplay sound effect at $CFCE-$CFCF. The decoder stops at the first $FF.
Generated character screen and sprite pointers. The loader copy carries alternating $FF/$00 fill in this page block; startup writes every displayed row and the raster writes sprite pointers.
extra: Main program and tables from file .5 at the loader handoff
Resident map, program and tables from file .4
Relocated playfield glyphs and alternate animation image from file .3

comments.text: Initialize VIC bank and display geometry, seed the pseudo-random state from the raster and prepare the sprite order before opening the title screen.
Restore five lives, clear the three instrument override bytes and draw the title. Set stage zero and the lance before entering stage setup.
Load the stage's camera limits, start position and palette. The retry path at $08B0 retains those values and redraws the stage with a fresh 2:59 timer.

Update audio, wait for the next raster tick and apply Arthur's input. If a whole tile of scroll is pending, move the objects, reorder sprites and refresh the map before testing objects and collisions.
Clear contact impulses, update weapons and actors, move and re-sort sprites, then decrement the timer. The flags at $3591 and $3594 request a stage advance or loss of life.
Increment stage index $3536. At four, run the rescue sequence at $0DA1 and start again from stage zero.
Decrement the life counter and retry the same stage while it remains nonzero. The final life leads to high-score entry and the reset path at $087E.
Compare the two packed score bytes with the incumbent records from the bottom up, moving their score and eight-character name together. Ask for a name only when the new record qualifies.
Convert the name cursor sprite's grid-aligned position into a $F400 screen address. Save the selected glyph in $35A9.
Place the joystick cursor sprite, fill the eight name cells with spaces and reset the letter index.
Read four active-low direction bits at $DC00 and set the cursor's signed velocities within the keyboard limits.
Clear each cursor velocity when its coordinate reaches the next 16-pixel grid boundary.
Switch to the short music score and render the title-alphabet prompt and keyboard. Tick the cursor and fire selection until the chosen symbol is ED.
Prompt and letter grid in the panel's glyph encoding. $FF starts the next row and $FE ends the full layout. The last cells are erase and end.
On a new fire press, read the cursor's glyph. ED exits, the left arrow erases the previous cell, and other glyphs append to the eight-character name.
Switch to backdrop number five and draw seven ranked names and scores into $F400 screen RAM. The row helpers take a screen destination at $FB and a record number in X.
Copy the four custom glyph codes for record X from $0D10 to the screen at ($FB), returning X unchanged.
Copy eight glyph codes from the selected name at $0D30 to the screen destination at $FB.
Convert the four packed decimal nibbles of record X to glyph numbers by adding $58. The store at $0D0B falls through to the X restore at $0D0D.
Common digit-writer tail which restores X from the stack and returns after printing the final digit.
Eight four-cell ordinal templates, 1ST through 8TH padded with glyph $66. The high-score page at $0C53 draws seven rows.
Eight-character names in the panel alphabet. The retail seed starts with CHRIS, then MUSICMAN, ELITE, CAPCOM, ALISTAIR, DAVE, KAY and a blank slot.
Second name entry. $0982 writes shifted eight-glyph records using this base while inserting a new score.
Two packed-decimal bytes per record, most significant first. The renderer appends two zero cells, so the first seed $0050 appears as 005000.
First score's low byte and base for the low-byte column of the score table. The caller doubles the rank to read successive records.
Insertion writes the high score byte one record later through this indexed base.
Insertion writes the low byte one record later through this base, keeping the remaining score pairs in rank order.
Count down $359D, reload it at 50 and write the current continue digit to $F5F3 when the slower seconds counter changes.
Select the ending backdrop, initialize two sprite slots, stamp the rescue message on the screen and update the scene until sprite 1 reaches X zero.
Thirty-seven panel glyphs spelling WELL DONE YOU HAVE SAVED THE PRINCESS, copied to $F4C9 by the ending sequence.
Temporarily select the title palette, clear logical sprites, copy two prompt strings and initialize the countdown to nine.
GAME OVER in the panel alphabet with a trailing $FF sentinel.
PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE. The copy at $0E55 stops at the sentinel $FF at $0E98.
Draw the title backdrop and logo sprites, tick the sound engine and test active-low port 2 fire. On timer expiry, show the high-score table and then return to the title.
Set up six consecutive sprite images $C0–$C5 at Y=$50 and X=$78 onward, separated by 24 pixels.

Decrement the 50-update prescaler at $359D and subtract a second in decimal mode. Borrow from minutes at zero seconds, or set the death flag on minute underflow. Convert digits to panel glyphs at $F6FF and $F701–$F702.
Select the death state when the minutes byte underflows. The death animation subsequently runs through the regular player update.
Add A to the low packed score byte in decimal mode. Carry increments the high byte and awards a life when it becomes $05.
Turn the two packed-decimal score bytes into four consecutive digits at $F719–$F71C.
Read the vertical travel limit pair and initial camera row and Arthur Y from four stage-indexed tables at $2919–$2928. Set the initial camera column to zero.
Await raster ticks, process Arthur movement, advance the sprites and redraw the map until Arthur reaches X=$97. Then clear the vertical scroll delta.
Allocate a slot for a jar sprite with type $0F and image $6C, then link it to its parent slot in $34D2.
Check an entity's X page and bounding window against Arthur's position. Two crouching poses tighten the upper Y bound from 20 pixels to 12. Return $FF on contact and zero otherwise.
Check the live projectile and compare its X page plus its X/Y window against entity X. Clear the projectile slot on a hit unless weapon number five is equipped.
Change slot X to type seven, zero its velocities and age, and request effect seven. The new handler advances the dissolve images.
Search all ordinary slots for type $0B with parent X. Put each matching part into the same break animation as the parent.
Queue effect seven, set sprite image $7D and type eight, and clear velocities and age for the flash-and-remove sequence.
Use the actor-type table at $121F to decide whether to test overlap. When the damage latch is zero, kick Arthur back and change his pose base by $40, then set the latch to $96.
Walk ordinary slots 13 through 0. Retire out-of-bounds actors except type-$0B followers. Increment age, check contact damage and dispatch the current type.
Thirty-two handler pointers indexed by actor type at $34A2. $116C calls via the indirect JMP at $1E6B and the selected handler's RTS returns to the update loop.
High byte of the first update pointer. $11AF indexes the odd bytes of the interleaved update pointer table.
Thirty-two actor-type flags controlling whether removing an offscreen slot clears the encounter's alive bit. $1191 tests this table when retiring actors.
Thirty-two actor-type flags read by $1129. Zero skips the damage check and one makes the actor eligible to hurt Arthur.
When Arthur overlaps the item, queue effect four, restore his armored pose base to $40 and clear the actor slot.
Flicker between image $7E and the blank image $FE. At ages $40 and $80, create two other flame slots above this one with staggered ages.
Flicker the upper flame between $7E and $FE using two random bits. Age wrap to zero removes the segment.
Assign $B8 during ages $10–$17 and $B9 during $90–$97. Try to allocate a projectile on multiples of $40, then run the shared velocity and hit logic.
Index the paired horizontal and vertical velocity tables by age divided by eight. A shot places a break animation in a reserved empty slot and advances the hit count. At ten hits spawn the key.
Thirty-two signed X steps used by $130E, indexed by the segment age divided by eight.
Thirty-two signed Y steps used by $1314, indexed with the same phase as the X table.

When Y velocity is nonzero or age is zero, select $B0 or $B1, set fall speed to one and test projectile contact. A hit scores 100. With no hit, an age multiple of 32 selects a new signed horizontal speed.

Use age low seven bits to select launch, retract and damage phases. Launch a type-nine projectile when the mouth image advances. At six recorded hits score 200 and destroy the actor and its type-$18 partner.
Stop the key's descent below a stage-derived line. An overlap clears its slot, sets the key-held flag and requests effect one.
Carry Arthur with the actor's velocities and place him nine pixels above it on contact. The initial contact starts the grouped type-$16 platform drop.
Reverse vertical velocity at $5A and $A0. Share the platform's movement with Arthur when he overlaps it and reset the contact latch as he leaves.

Choose two adjoining sprite images, follow Arthur horizontally when within the Y band and shoot a horizontally or vertically moving projectile when outside it. Ten projectile contacts score 400 and start the break animation.
Four sprite indices selected by signed horizontal speed and one age bit. The attached lower sprite uses the next image number.
Wait 32 ticks before beginning the terrain-driven walk. Pick a direction toward Arthur once landed, alternate images from $16B5 and score 200 on a hit.
Four sprite indices selected by horizontal direction and animation phase in $163E.
Alternate two sprite images and select new signed X and Y motion every 32 age steps. A projectile hit adds 200 and starts its dissolve.
Pair of sprite indices selected by bit three of actor age.
Contact consumes this item and either adds 200 or selects a new weapon from its sprite number. The $67 item cycles through four colours until picked up.
Four VIC colour values selected by two bits of the pickup actor's age.
A shot breaks this actor and awards 200. Otherwise it fires a new type-$11 projectile at its 128-step phase zero and updates movement in a later phase.
Drive vertical velocity from the 16-entry wave at $1830 and award 200 on a hit.
Sixteen signed Y steps from minus four to plus four and back, indexed by actor age divided by four.
Turn after 150 age steps. Carry Arthur when his centre is above the platform within the one-sided contact window, using the shared response at $18B3.
Reverse after 145 age steps and test Arthur with the regular overlap box. Clear the riding latch when he leaves.
Transfer platform X and Y velocities to Arthur's contact impulses. Put him eleven pixels above the platform and clear his initial jump state on first contact.
Copy the linked actor's velocities into this sprite's slot, or clear the slot if the parent is absent or breaking.
Follow the parent while it is alive. Once released, accelerate downwards until landing, then become a bonus or the next weapon in the cycle.
Two chances for sprite $6D, one for $6E and one zero selecting the next weapon.
Delay the movement cycle while the actor is above $46. Apply table velocities, loop at the X sentinel, and spawn an aimed projectile as the age wraps. Four hits award 400.
Allocate and aim a projectile toward Arthur, then use image $97 and colour $0E for the child.
Increment the shared hit counter. At four, add 400 and replace the enemy with its break animation.
The signed X velocity of each 16-tick phase, ending with $FF to restart the movement cycle.
Sixteen signed Y velocities paired with the active X phases in $1A02.

Fire an aimed projectile at the age boundary. During the jump and landing phases, animate linked boss pieces and accept projectile hits on either part. On the seventh hit, score 500 and spawn the key.
Fetch an ordinary sprite slot, make it a key of type $17 and start its descent at screen position ($A0,$32).
Alternate the explosion sprite $7D and the blank sprite $FE. Release the slot when its age reaches 60.
Choose the next dissolve image every four age steps and clear the slot at the $FF marker.
Six consecutive sprite indices $6F–$74, followed by the terminator which removes the actor.
Use one sinking frame for eight age ticks and remove the slot at the sentinel.
Sprite images $66, $65 and $64 shown in that order before clearing the slot.
Run three emerging frames and switch to the walking state. Choose direction from the spawn X and, on a one-in-eight random result, attach a jar.
Reverse of the sink images, followed by $FF to change the actor to walking type four.
Probe footing, choose direction from the sprite pose, animate the stride and test projectile contact. Start the sink sequence when footing vanishes or the byte age wraps.
Signed horizontal step table addressed by bit one of the zombie sprite index.
Wait until age $50 before flying left. Use the raster tick to drive the wing frames and slight Y variation. One hit scores 100.
Four sprite indices $69–$6B for the wing cycle, indexed by the raster count divided by eight.
Eight signed vertical velocity offsets, including one downward and one upward movement.
Select the sprite from the age and shoot from a new ordinary slot every 64 steps. A projectile hit scores 300 and switches to the break flash.
Allocate a child at the actor's screen position. Halve the absolute deltas to Arthur until X is below four and Y below three, then restore their original signs as the velocities.
Eight pointer entries, keeping $5D through six phases before advancing through $5E and $5F.
Search slots 13 down to zero for a zero actor type. Return its index in X, or $FF when all ordinary slots are occupied.
Same reverse free-slot search as $1D96, returning the slot in Y for callers that preserve their parent actor in X.
Four little-endian table addresses for encounter map columns, in stage-number order.
First high-byte entry in the interleaved X pointer table, indexed by stage times two.
Four little-endian table addresses for encounter map rows.
First high-byte entry in the little-endian Y pointer array read at $1DDB.
Four little-endian table addresses for the encounter initializer numbers.
First high-byte entry in the type-pointer table read at $1DE7.
Choose three parallel tables of map X, map Y and encounter type from stage-indexed address tables. Clear both encounter-state arrays until the X sentinel $FF.
Compare stored encounter coordinates with the viewport and skip entries already present or consumed. For a newly visible entry, look up its actor definition and ask for a free slot.
Jump indirectly via $00FB to the selected handler. Its RTS returns to the caller of this dispatch stub.
Graveyard and forest spawn columns, one byte per entry and an $FF end marker.
Graveyard and forest spawn rows, matching the order of the columns immediately before this table.
Graveyard and forest encounter types. Each value indexes the initializer word table at $1FAA.
Ice palace and village spawn columns, terminated by $FF.
Ice palace and village spawn rows, parallel to the stage two column array.
Ice palace and village initializer numbers, indexed by the same encounter position as the rows and columns.
Labyrinth and castle spawn columns, including the last marker $FF.
Labyrinth and castle Y tile positions, one for each stage four encounter column.
Labyrinth and castle initializer numbers, parallel to the position arrays.
Cloud and bridge spawn columns with $FF after the last entry.
Cloud and bridge Y tile positions, parallel to the stage three X array.
Cloud and bridge initializer numbers, one for every position pair.
Twenty-five initializer pointers, indexed by doubling the encounter type. Type $18 is the midstage checkpoint initializer at $1FFB.
High byte column of the little-endian spawn handler table. The reader at $1E49 indexes the odd bytes by encounter type times two.
Convert the encounter's tile coordinates to screen coordinates, set its encounter flags and make the sprite an armor pickup with pointer $FD.
Compute the encounter's screen position. Once the camera has approached it within the horizontal and vertical thresholds, save the new restart column, row and Arthur Y, then free the temporary slot.
RTS target for actor types with no per-update behaviour or no spawn setup.
Clear $D01B, placing all hardware sprites in front of background graphics.
Retire ordinary actors and create a dragon head in slot nine plus nine body sprites with delayed phases. Set the stage fight flag and reset the shared hit tally.
Nine body seed ages, stepped by six so adjacent sprites move through their velocity cycle at different times.
Nine initial body X coordinates for the boss initializer at $2079.
Nine initial body Y coordinates for the boss initializer at $207F.
Project the map encounter into a slot, store its encounter ID, set sprite $B2 and type $19, and seed its phase with the random generator.
Set up a stationary hazard of type $1D at the supplied map position with image $7E, yellow colour and age zero.
Place two type-$18 sprites one 21-pixel row apart with images $B4 and $B3. Both share the encounter index and get separate random phases.
Initialize the ordinary vertical platform, then replace its velocity with zero and its type with $16, which waits for contact.
Set the encountered slot to image $AF and type $15 with an initial downward velocity of one.
Set the parent to type $14 with image $A0 and allocate its second image $A1 one sprite row below. Save the child index in the parent and the parent index in the follower.
Allow a type-$13 spawn when the raster tick is divisible by 64 and the secondary two-bit counter wraps. Set heading and age to zero.
On tick multiples of 128, place a type-$12 enemy. One random value out of eight attaches a jar below it when a second slot is free.
On a raster tick multiple of 64, send a left-moving enemy from high-X page with random Y and age. An optional jar follows ten pixels below.
Set up type $1C with image $BB. Add 16 to its low X byte for the $BC follower and copy its X page unchanged. The follower writes use Y from the slot search without checking the $FF result.
Place the encountered type-$0C enemy with image $75, starting age $23 and leftward speed of one.
Queue effect five and place a type-$0A parent with image $76. When slots are available add two type-$0B followers below and to the right.
Start the boss encounter with image $98 and set the fight flags. Allocate up to three follower sprites using $99, $9A and $9B.
Set the allocated child to type $0B, inherit the parent's X page and link it back to slot X.
On every 64th raster tick, initialize a left-moving flyer at a random phase from the wave table and optionally attach a jar.
Allow a type-five emergence when the raster count is divisible by 128 and a random X yields a terrain tile underfoot. Choose the colour from the stage.
On the raster tick byte wrapping to zero, place a bird beyond the right of the screen and 20 pixels above Arthur with age $50.
Allocate the map-based bird with sprite $68, colour $0A and type three. Mark the encounter as active.
Run the type-two pickup initializer and select the point bonus image $6D.
Set the persistent pickup to sprite $67, type two and colour $0E. Keep the map encounter index on its slot.
Place the map encounter two pixels above its normal projection and use plant sprite $5D with type one.
Convert encounter Y's tile coordinates to logical slot X's pixel position relative to the current camera, applying the per-stage vertical adjustment.
Four pixel offsets added by $2646 after projecting a spawn's tile row into screen coordinates.
Convert pixel X/Y and X high bit to a position in the resident 256-column map. Index the terrain flag table at $2E2A with the returned tile code.
Increase projectile age and look up an update address by projectile state in $269E. Tail-jump to the selected routine.
Seven state pointers for the weapon logic. States one and three share the terrain-sensitive handler at $276B.
High byte of the first indirect weapon handler address, read with a stride of two at $2695.
Six VIC sprite colours indexed by weapon number. The same table supplies the travelling weapon at $270A and the panel sprite at $32E9.
Initial rightward horizontal projectile velocity, indexed by weapon number. A left throw negates the selected speed.
Sprite pointers for a right-facing projectile and for the weapon display. The left throw chooses the next pointer in the pair.
Clear the held-fire latch when fire is up or Arthur enters the death state.
If port 2 fire is down, the latch is clear and Arthur is off the ladder, create a projectile at a pose-dependent offset from Arthur. Set its colour, speed and frame from the weapon tables.
Alternate two frames at $2769, zero movement and release the slot when its age reaches 12.
Two sprite indices alternated by bit 2 of the projectile age counter.
Check for solid terrain just above a moving projectile. When it hits terrain, undo the last X movement and enter impact state six. When it misses, remove it at age $19.
On the first terrain hit, stop the projectile and mark its age with bit 7. Select the eight-entry burning frame cycle until the lower seven age bits reach $1E.
Sprite pointer cycle for the stationary burning projectile. The direction and low age bits select the entry.
Check for solid terrain while the projectile is younger than 25 updates, converting a hit to the impact state. Release it when it ages out.
Apply the throw pose, keep sprite $5C and clear this slot once age reaches $19.
Alternate the weapon's two frames and increase vertical velocity every eighth age step. Return the terrain flags beneath its current position.
During the first ten updates of the throw, select an upright or crouching pose from the joystick, direction and age.
Clear the logical objects, place Arthur at the requested stage start, restore armor and zero the movement, ladder and transition latches.
Initial vertical tile offset for the four stages, in stage order $00, $6C, $12, $3D.
Arthur's initial screen Y in pixels for each stage, loaded by $0FD7 into $3597.
Four vertical camera row minima used in the upward test at $2F82.
Four vertical camera row maxima used to bound the downward scroll test at $2F94.
Select the $C000 bank and $F400 screen. Enable the eight multicolor sprites, set shared colors, turn on text multicolor and set the border black.
Reset all sixteen logical slots via $307B, including the slots reserved for Arthur and the projectile.
Colour register $D022 for four stages, title or continue, and high-score or ending backdrop.
Colour register $D023 for the six scene settings selected by $3536.
Low $D018 bits for the six scene settings. $0E selects glyphs at $F800 and $0C selects glyphs at $F000 in bank $C000.
Set the stage palette and character generator, select the row-fill tables for this scene, and fill each row of screen and colour RAM. Restore the panel labels and high score afterwards.
Low byte patched into the indexed colour row-table load at $29C9.
High byte of the patched colour address. $29D3–$29F4 repeat its nibble across 40 columns for each row.
Low byte of the scene-dependent pointer operand in the screen fill load at $29CE.
High byte of the patched tile row-table address. The row loop advances X after filling forty character cells with one tile code.
Per-row screen defaults for the gameplay scenes, using the playfield blank above and the panel blank below. The setup repeats each byte across 40 columns.
Per-row blank glyphs for the title, scores or rescue scene. $297A uses this table when the panel font occupies the screen.
Twenty-five colour nibbles repeated across the rows of the graveyard screen by $29CC.
One VIC colour nibble per row for the ice palace and town stage settings.
Row colours for the labyrinth and castle stage.
Row colours for the clouds and fire bridge stage.
Per-row ink for the title and continue prompt.
Per-row ink used for the high-score or rescue backdrop.
Six little-endian pointers to the per-row colour fill for each value of $3536. $29AD uses the scene index times two.
Odd-byte alias for the high bytes of the six scene colour pointers, loaded at $29B3.
Parallel six-pointer table for the repeated initial screen character of each row. There are separate templates for gameplay and the text backdrops.
High-byte alias for the screen row-fill addresses. $29BF uses this base with the doubled scene index.
Copy the $FF-terminated TIME, WEAPON and SCORE row to $F6F9 and the ten-cell TOP field to $F765.
Panel-alphabet template for TIME, WEAPON and SCORE, with digit placeholders and an $FF terminator.
Ten custom glyphs for TOP and the high-score placeholders. The length is fixed at ten by $2B03.
Cycle four animation phases from the walking counter, adding the current left or right pose base.
Four entries indexed by elapsed death ticks divided by eight. The final frame is repeated.
Increase vertical velocity every fourth airborne tick up to seven. Test for falling beyond the lower limit before the terrain contact path.
Stop movement, switch to death animation and queue sound at the start of the sequence. At count 100 set the life-loss flag.
Dispatch Arthur's motion state. Select airborne, dying, ladder or ground movement. In ordinary movement, active-low bits from port 2 choose direction, jump and crouch.
Derive climb velocity directly from up and down, animate from Y position and stop climbing when the ladder probe at the feet leaves a ladder tile.
Advance Arthur right automatically with the key, bypass normal stick motion and flag a stage advance after reaching the far side of the door.
Use joystick left and right for horizontal speed and facing. For an up press, prioritize a ladder tile above and otherwise latch a jump with vertical speed minus four.
Clear the sustained-up latch after the joystick's up bit returns high.
With down held, probe below Arthur to choose ladder descent or a crouch pose. The ground test below starts a fall if there is neither platform contact nor solid terrain.
Probe the tile in the attempted direction. Apply background priority from bit two. Stop upward motion at solid tiles and snap downwards motion to a tile row on landing.
Add the current armor-dependent frame base to the pose. While the contact countdown runs, either switch to death when unarmored or alternate a blank frame.
Clear the coarse scroll request and apply horizontal and vertical Arthur motion, moving the camera when appropriate.
One flag byte per map glyph. Bit zero is tested for solid footing and bit one for ladders. The table is indexed by the tile read in $2653.
Four offsets subtracted from the aligned Arthur Y when landing. They are indexed by stage at $2DC2.
Clear the VIC column-width and row-height bits, putting the playfield in 38-column, 24-row mode for scrolling.
Copy 19 rows of 40 tile codes to $F400. Source is $4000 plus row offset times 256 plus the column offset, and the self-modified source operand advances one page per row.
Low byte of the self-modified source address at $2F5A, loaded from the camera's tile column.
High byte of the patched source address, advanced at $2F63. The adjacent instruction stores the loaded tile in the current screen row.
Low byte of the $2F5D screen destination operand, advanced by 40 after each displayed row.
High byte of the patched destination address. $2F71 carries into it after adding the row stride. The loop ends when the low byte reaches $F8.
Sum the signed vertical movement and contact impulse. At a scroll threshold inside the stage's vertical limits, update character and pixel camera offsets instead of moving the sprite.
Move the sprite until it reaches the camera centre or a scroll limit. Otherwise put the motion into the camera's signed pixel and tile offsets and request a coarse redraw after crossing a tile.
Remove actor X by marking its type zero and setting it to the offscreen parking coordinates. Clear its movement and linked-slot index.
Advance Arthur by the two committed velocities. Move other active slots by their own signed velocities minus camera motion, toggling their X page when crossing a byte boundary.
Shift the two-byte state at $3450–$3451, then mix the shifted values with XOR and an add that uses the shift carry. Return the new low byte in A.
Seed the random state from $D012 and twice that value. Wait for a nonzero doubled raster value before returning.
Sort the 16 slot indices by Y using passes in both directions. Precompute the hardware X-high bit for the later eight slots before the raster routine reuses a sprite.
Write identity slot numbers 0 through 15 to $4B–$5A before the first Y sort.
Wait for the byte at $3448 to change. The panel raster handler increments it at $3222.
Stop CIA1 timer A, bank out KERNAL and BASIC, write RAM NMI and IRQ vectors, and enable VIC raster IRQs with an initial line of $C6.
Immediate RTI for the game's RAM NMI vector at $FFFA.
Save A, X and Y to zero page then jump through the current raster-handler pointer at $3446.
Change display fine scroll and graphics mode at the bottom of the playfield, assign the panel font at $F000, increment the frame tick, and schedule $3243.
Swap alternate glyph bytes on tick multiples of 16. Place the weapon indicator and as many life sprites as the remaining life count permits, then schedule the playfield handler at $32FE.
Apply camera fine scroll and playfield character base. Program the first eight sprite positions, colours and image pointers in sorted Y order, then schedule the first reuse.
Replace a hardware sprite with the next sorted logical sprite. Cluster near-equal Y positions into one IRQ and schedule the next group five raster lines before its Y.
Schedule the panel switch at raster $C5, acknowledge the VIC interrupt, restore the saved registers and return.
One set bit for each hardware sprite, used to merge its ninth X coordinate into $D010.
Inverses of the per-sprite masks at $3436, used by the multiplex handler before replacing a ninth X bit.
Low byte of the indirect jump address used by the IRQ dispatcher.
High byte of the next raster subhandler, selected by the preceding subhandler.
Incremented by $3222 at the playfield-to-panel split. The main loop waits for a different value at $319D.
Horizontal pixel scroll within the current tile column, used by $3307 for $D016.
Vertical pixel scroll within the current tile row. It affects both graphics positioning and coordinate projection.
Low byte of the resident map origin selected by the horizontal camera position.
Offset from map page $40 of the first visible tile row.
Signed horizontal delta removed from other sprites' coordinates when the camera scrolls.
Signed vertical camera delta subtracted from actors' Y. The gap before $3450 separates the camera state from the random seed.
Low random-state byte, seeded from the VIC raster and mixed at $30FA.
High random-state byte rotated by $30FE.
Start of the X-low array for ordinary actor slots. The name-entry cursor and end scene also use slot zero.
X-low values for ordinary slots 1–13. The rescue scene writes slot one directly.
Position low byte of the weapon projectile, slot 14.
Low byte of Arthur's horizontal position, corresponding to logical slot 15.
Start of the Y-position array and base for the sprite-order comparisons at $3126.
Y coordinates for ordinary slots 1–13. During the title, $0EF3 places the logo sprites in slots 0–5.
Vertical position of the travelling weapon in slot 14.
Arthur's screen Y in pixels, used for terrain probes and object contacts.
Start of the ordinary slots' X-page flags. The drawing code masks these values into $D010.
X-page flags for ordinary slots 1–13, stored as zero or $FF.
Ninth horizontal bit of the current weapon projectile as a zero or $FF mask.
Arthur's X-page flag. Collision helpers compare it with another sprite's flag before comparing low bytes.
Beginning of the sixteen logical sprite colour entries.
VIC colour values for ordinary logical sprites 1–13, copied to the hardware during multiplexing.
VIC colour nibble loaded from the equipped weapon's colour table.
Colour selected for Arthur in the current logical sprite slot. Stage reset sets it to $0E.
Base of the sixteen current sprite pointers. Raster handlers translate a logical slot into the image at bank $C000 plus pointer times 64.
Image field for ordinary slots 1–13, independently changed by the actors' animation handlers.
Image number selected for the projectile, its left-facing variant, or its impact animation.
Image number from the pose and armour base, with blanking during the damage interval.
Actor type index at slot zero and base of the slot allocator's state test.
Update-handler numbers for ordinary slots 1–13. Zero marks a free slot.

VIC multicolor sprite images $40–$4F in bank $C000. Each 64-byte slot contains 21 rows of three bytes and one byte outside the sprite raster. $40 supplies the spare-life icon.
VIC sprite images $50–$5F. The weapon pointer table at $26B8 includes $54, $56, $58, $5A and $5C, with the next image used for the left-facing throw.
VIC sprite images $60–$6F in RAM beneath colour memory. The sprite pointer in a cell at $F7F8–$F7FF chooses a 64-byte image from the $C000 VIC bank.
VIC sprite images $70–$7F in RAM beneath the CIAs and expansion I/O. The game chooses $7E or $7F for the stationary fire animation at $2803.
VIC sprite images $80–$8F, 16 records of 64 bytes starting at $E000. CPU port $35 leaves the KERNAL region mapped to RAM.
VIC sprite images $90–$9F. The impact sequence at $2769 alternates $9E and $9F before clearing the projectile.
VIC sprite images $A0–$AF relocated to $E800 by the loader. Each row has twelve multicolor pixels packed two bits per pixel.
VIC sprite images $B0–$BF at $EC00, selected when the raster copies logical image numbers from the slot array at $3492.
VIC image slots $C0–$CF share this address range with glyph indices $00–$7F of the $F000 character generator. The title logo uses sprites $C0–$C5 and the digits and letters occupy glyphs $58–$7F.
First 128 eight-byte glyphs of the $F800 playfield set. Most stages select this set via the low bits of $D018 at $331A.
Upper half of the $F800 glyph set, ending before the RAM vectors. The raster also selects image slots in this memory for sprites, including the panel's $FE placeholder.
Eight initial glyph bytes for index $FC in the $F800 set. The raster handler at $3261 swaps them with the next eight bytes.
Alternate eight-byte image exchanged with glyph $FC on frame ticks whose low nibble is zero.
